title: Issue mutation call path (view → facade → logic → model)
answers: Where is issue status/assignee mutated in error tracking?
How does resolving an error tracking issue flow through the backend?
Where do merge and split of issues live?
body:
EB = products/error_tracking/backend.
Hops: EB/presentation/views/issues.py:ErrorTrackingIssueViewSet → EB/facade/issues.py (thin wrapper) → EB/logic/issue_mutations.py.
- update_issue: status/severity/name/description. Resolve/reopen are status changes here, not separate functions.
- merge_issues → models.py:ErrorTrackingIssue.merge (select_for_update in id order, raw SQL fingerprint rewrite, moves spike events, _adopt_source_assignee_on_merge). split_issue → ErrorTrackingIssue.split.
- assign_issue → _assign_one; bulk_update_issues supports set_status and assign.
- set_issue_cohort is a bare update_or_create: no activity log, no event.
- API only allows active/resolved/suppressed: WRITABLE_ISSUE_STATUSES in views/issues.py.
- update_issue: save + activity log + lifecycle event registration in one transaction.atomic(); sync_issues_to_clickhouse runs after the block (not on_commit), so a raise leaves Postgres committed.

search: Issue mutations follow view → facade → logic → model path; ErrorTrackingIssueViewSet calls facade, which calls functions like update_issue, merge_issues, assign_issue in products/error_tracking/backend/logic/issue_mutations.py. Updates (status/severity/name/description) are transactional with activity log and lifecycle event, but WRITABLE_ISSUE_STATUSES restricts API to active/resolved/suppressed. Exception: set_issue_cohort omits activity log; merge_issues uses select_for_update and raw SQL. sync_issues_to_clickhouse runs after transaction block (not on_commit), leaving Postgres committed on exceptions. Applies to issue update/merge/split/assign/bulk workflows.
